text: DSH Advisor 是面向 DSH 会话的第二意见审查插件：它按已完成步骤的节奏创建独立审查子会话，让审查者用只读工具重新查看 Executor 的近期工作，并将具体发现作为建议送回会话。它提供可配置的审查模型、间隔、上下文上限和超时；Web 会话页可查看审查状态、历史、队列与用量，并调整配置或恢复暂停的审查。适合希望在 DSH 编码会话中获得额外核对、减少遗漏的用户。需要在 DSH 中配置审查专用的 provider 和 model；插件不会自动沿用 Executor 的模型。

DSH Advisor runs scheduled second-opinion reviews in DSH sessions. A separate reviewer reads recent work with read-only tools and returns concrete advice. Configure its model, cadence, context limit and timeout; the Web tab shows status and settings. Choose a dedicated provider and model.
想让 DSH 在编码过程中定期帮我复核已经完成的工作。
DSH 能不能让另一个审查会话重新读文件，检查 Executor 做得对不对？
希望在会话里看到独立审查发现的问题和建议。
我想给自动代码复核单独选模型，并限制它的上下文和运行时间。
Can I get periodic, independent checks of the work produced in a DSH session?
I want a session tab that shows review status and lets me adjust the review settings.
DSH Advisor 的功能「定期第二意见」：按配置的完成步骤间隔创建独立审查会话，审查者重新读取近期工作并提交具体意见。
DSH Advisor 的功能「会话内建议」：审查子会话可提交发现，插件将建议整理为 Executor 会话中的消息，供后续工作查看。
DSH Advisor 的功能「Web 状态与配置页」：在对话视图提供 Advisor 标签页，显示会话审查状态；页面通过状态、模型目录和配置路由读取信息并保存设置。
DSH Advisor 的功能「可调审查节奏」：配置可指定专用 provider 与 model、每次审查的步数间隔、上下文 token 上限和超时；enabled 开启时必须提供模型路由。
DSH 的审查一直失败时，我希望能从会话页面查看状态并手动恢复。
I need a separate model to review recent session work and send findings back to the conversation.

@wweir/dsh-advisor README · @wweir/dsh-advisor：English | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

An automatic second opinion for DeepSeek Harness sessions.

On a configurable step rhythm, a **restricted sub-agent** re-reads the
Executor's recent work with read-only tools. Concrete defects are recorded and
delivered to the Executor's inbox; when there is nothing to point at, the
reviewer stays silent — silence is the normal outcome, not a failure.

@wweir/dsh-advisor README · What it does for you：- **Catches hallucinations.** The reviewer reads the actual files (read-only):
  changes claimed but not made, APIs that do not exist, values never written.
  The note points at the mismatch while the work is fresh; delivery is
  advisory, interrupting only as configured.
- **Keeps sessions on track.** At most one review every N completed steps
  (default 8), never concurrently — a step boundary that arrives mid-review
  waits for the next cadence instead of stacking reviews. A step is one model
  call plus its tools, so one cadence covers work inside a long turn and work
  spread across many short turns; `everySteps: 0` turns automatic review off.
  Drift is reported inside the running turn; idle sessions can be woken by
  severe findings (budgeted, severity-gated). Silence is reported as a result,
  not an error.
- **Bounded cost.** The reviewer's context is a compiled two-zone projection,
  never a copy of the Executor's. The prompt is capped by the operator's
  `maxContextTokens` (64K by default) **and** by the reviewer model's own
  window: the host preamble, the model's output reserve and a margin are

@wweir/dsh-advisor README · Why：- **It verifies instead of guessing.** The reviewer opens the files the
  Executor actually touched, so a note points at a defect it looked at — not
  a pattern inferred from a transcript summary, which is all a
  transcript-only reviewer can ever offer.
- **The host's rules apply to the review itself.** Turn/step accounting, the
  tool pipeline, streaming, cancellation, persistence, and a real audit
  trail: the review is a session you can inspect, and its cost is reported
  usage, not an estimate.
- **Isolation is enforced, not promised.** One reviewer claim per process, a
  read-only tool surface, a protected-path guard deliberately stricter than
  the upstream advisor (workspace-root private keys and `.envrc` included),
  and no shared context with the Executor.
- **Delivery is accounted.** A **follow-up** note counts as delivered only when
  the host proves it was processed (that turn's model reply); an unconfirmed
  note is requeued, never silently dropped. A note steered into a running turn
  counts as delivered at the hand-off. Repetition is suppressed by finding
  identity plus similarity, with hash-based mutes.

@wweir/dsh-advisor README · Install：The package is a Cordis plugin (`dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`) and is
published on npm with a provenance attestation, so it installs like any other
profile bundle:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @wweir/dsh-advisor
```

A development checkout can be linked instead (`dsh plugin … add /path/to/checkout`);
its deploy path is described in `docs/OPERATIONS.md`.

@wweir/dsh-advisor README · Install：Then give it a model route. It is **disabled until a model is configured**, and
it never falls back to the Executor's model:

```yaml
- id: advisor
  name: '@wweir/dsh-advisor'
  config:
    enabled: true

A patch entry is **replaced, not merged**, per row id: an overlay that sets
only the extra instructions drops the model route, so the row loads **disabled**;
it fails loudly, with a validation error, only when the overlay also asks for
`enabled: true`.

@wweir/dsh-advisor README · Behaviour worth knowing：- **Trigger** — one cadence: a completed *step*, i.e. one model call plus the
  tools it ran. Steps are the host's progress unit, so the same counter covers
  work inside a long turn (which crosses no reply boundary for dozens of steps)
  and work spread across many short turns; there is no second, reply-based
  interval that could disagree with it. A review starts once `everySteps` steps
  (default 8) have accrued since the previous one finished. The cursor moves
  when a review *finishes*, so a slow review cannot chain into the next one; the
  counter and cursor are absolute and persisted, so a reload continues the
  cadence instead of forgiving the steps that accrued since the last review. A
  fresh session is first reviewed after a full cadence, not immediately. The
  turn's final answer starts no review of its own: the steps that produced it
  already had their chance, so the tail of a session that stops mid-cadence is
  reviewed by the next steps that accrue. Sub-agent sessions (including the
  review children) are never reviewed. Turns this plugin opened itself are never
  reviewed either.

@wweir/dsh-advisor README · Presentation of a delivered note：A review note is delivered as a chat notice attributed to the advisor.
Delivered while the Executor runs, it renders as a collapsed context row
that already carries the one-line summary
(`关注 · 仍适用 · …`). Delivered while the Executor is idle it wakes a turn, so
the chat draws its **turn-trigger card** — and upstream that card has no
advisor branch: it falls back to a generic "Execution requested" title and
shows no summary, leaving the note invisible until clicked.

@wweir/dsh-advisor README · Presentation of a delivered note：The local client patch `~/.wweir/bin/dsh-patch-advisor-note` (re-applied by
`~/.wweir/bin/dsh-install`) adds the missing branch to the vendored chat
bundle: the card says 「二审提醒」/ "Advisor review", shows the recorded
severity and summary on the collapsed row, and renders the note text itself
when expanded. It is a vendored file edit, so a DSH upgrade drops it until
`dsh-install` runs again.

@wweir/dsh-advisor README · Verification：```bash
pnpm run verify   # typecheck (src + tests), client types, the test suite, the host build
pnpm run build    # tsc: src/ -> lib/, which is what a linked profile loads
```

@wweir/dsh-advisor README · Verification：The package follows the DSH plugin shape: the host entry is `lib/index.js` (built
from `src/index.ts`), the web half is the hand-written bundle at
`client/index.js`, and `dsh.bundle.patch` points at `cordis.patch.yml`. Deploying
a linked checkout, including the no-restart hot reload and its verification
markers, is documented in `docs/OPERATIONS.md`.

@wweir/dsh-advisor README · Verification：Tests cover the pure policy layer, the dependency direction the host half is
built on, the web bundle's loader contract, and the runtime driven through a
fake port; the full chain needs a long-lived app, which `docs/OPERATIONS.md`
explains together with the deploy path.

@wweir/dsh-advisor README · Known limits：- The protected-path guard judges the path a read tool addresses. A search tool
  rooted at a subdirectory can still return the body of a protected file inside
  that subdirectory (for example a repo `.env`); the search-root ban covers the
  working directory itself, and result redaction is the second line of defence.
- The page persists its configuration as the full page-owned projection, so a
  restart reproduces what the tab showed. Fields outside that set (queue
  capacity, protected paths) stay owned by the config row and cannot be
  changed from the page.

@wweir/dsh-advisor README · Known limits：- Deferred-advice invalidation on log rewrite/compaction is not implemented; the
  boundary a concluded review advances lives in process memory, so a reload
  marks the whole transcript as new to the next review (it re-reads more, it
  never skips work).
- The reviewer reads files through the Executor's own agent-preset composition,
  so remote-asset file tools are not on its surface: work performed through a
  remote namespace cannot be verified by reading it, and such a review stays
  silent rather than judging a different filesystem. The protected-path guard
  resolves paths through the same host service the filesystem tools use.
- A follow-up the host accepts but never turns into a turn (for example an agent
  that is already closing) leaves its note visible as *awaiting confirmation*
  instead of falsely delivered; it is requeued by the next plugin load. A note
  steered into a running turn counts as delivered at the hand-off; the page's
